original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.
Extending a source-count census without naming a supplier/interface decision it could change; audit #2973 pruning concerns before relying on the affected predecessor exclusions.

actual_scope: On one explicit six-source length-42 floor word other than the PR #7037 witness, evaluate the same 903-pair predicate and record whether the masks (3, 5) and (0, 1, 3, 5) are realized. The word is the block completion 3,5,0,1,2^7,4^7,0^6,1^6,3^6,5^6.
scope_change_reason: The catalogue card asks for one new connector operation. This package keeps the unsigned dirty connector alphabet fixed and answers open question 1 of PR #7037: whether one other length-42 floor word realizes both non-weight-3 masks missed by the recorded witness. A new operation is not the missing step. The family expansion gate is not invoked.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the recursive-interface schedule. A depth-two block needs both masks, and the #7037 census shows only that one witness misses them. Exhibiting another floor word that realizes both separates that miss from the floor-word hypotheses. No supplier, consumer, or selected kappa changes.
stop_rule: Stop once one named floor word other than the #7037 witness has been evaluated on all 903 pairs for these two masks, whether it realizes both or misses at least one. Do not replace the question with a census of every floor word or with a depth-two block claim.
evidence: The block word 350122222224444444000000111111333333555555 calls each of six sources seven times. A direct prefix count shows that any word whose first two letters are {3,5} and whose next two are {0,1} realizes (3,5) at (0,2) and (0,1,3,5) at (0,4); all four such prefixes are checked. The exhaustive 903-pair census of this one completion finds exactly three realizing pairs for (3,5), namely (0,2), (0,30) and (1,36), and exactly three for (0,1,3,5), namely (0,4), (0,11) and (0,18). The same predicate realizes neither mask on the #7037 witness or on the adjacent transposition of positions 1 and 2. A one-letter edit is rejected. This is not a depth-two block and not an unrestricted existence claim.

open_questions.question: Which of the other 61 nonzero masks does this same block word miss?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A depth-two block needs every nonzero mask. Realizing (3, 5) and (0, 1, 3, 5) does not decide the rest, and these two masks are not a block.
open_questions.first_step: Run the same 903-pair predicate on this one word and list the masks with no realizing pair.
open_questions.blocked_by: The checker discards every mask other than the two named targets. An exhaustive census of every floor word would be a different claim.

open_questions.question: Does any adjacent transposition of the #7037 witness, other than the swap of positions 1 and 2, realize both masks?
open_questions.why_it_matters: That one transposition is a floor word and misses both, so the positive block word is not a one-step move of the recorded witness. The domain has 41 adjacent positions.
open_questions.first_step: Evaluate the 903-pair predicate on each adjacent swap of distinct letters and record, for these two masks only, whether both are realized.
open_questions.blocked_by: Only the swap of positions 1 and 2 is checked here.
